comparator.route: Earth Sciences major with Consultancy for Sustainability as the Year 2 practice project
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–2027 curriculum specifies a common 60-EC first year, two interdisciplinary projects plus 51 EC in the selected major in Year 2, and a final interdisciplinary project plus 54 EC in the selected major in Year 3. The public programme page lists 21 formal majors but does not publish a dependable course-level EC split for each major. For this generic normalized target, Earth Sciences is selected by the neutral first-listed-major tie-break before UCR comparison. Its 105 EC is therefore preserved as two year-level aggregate components. The Year 2 project choice is Consultancy for Sustainability, the first listed option under the same neutral rule. The Year 3 major aggregate includes the bachelor thesis; no separate thesis EC is stated on the cited public curriculum.

alternatives.label: Natural, Social & Interdisciplinary Sciences
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines UCR courses across all six clusters to mirror Bèta-gamma’s defining integration of natural science, social science and humanities without implying that one discipline is the whole programme.
alternatives.concept: A broad UCR Liberal Arts and Sciences pathway integrating natural science, social science, humanities, methods and communication around complex societal questions.
progression: Gateway courses in sustainability, brain and behaviour, research methods, programming, politics and communication precede advanced work across environment, psychology, leadership, data, cognition, history and media. PPD is in Year 1, prerequisites and term availability are satisfied, and the curriculum contains substantial 300-level depth.

alternatives.label: AI, Technology & Society
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule combines UCR’s full data and intelligent-systems progression with psychology, communication and social-science framing, so the label states both its computational centre and its societal lens.
alternatives.concept: A computational Bèta-gamma-style direction joining programming, data science, mathematics and AI with cognition, communication and social analysis.
progression: Research, mathematics, data and database foundations precede programming-intensive software, robotics, algorithms, optimisation, reinforcement learning and deep learning. Programming and Mathematical Methods precede every formal dependent, and all courses are offered in their assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest pathway, this alternative concentrates on a continuous programming, data, mathematics and artificial-intelligence spine while retaining explicit human and social context.

alternatives.label: Sustainability, Cities & Public Policy
alternatives.concept: An Earth- and society-facing direction linking sustainability, cities, environmental change, governance, economics and applied social research.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule integrates sustainability, delta and environmental study with sociology, politics and economics, accurately describing its Earth-systems, urban and policy focus.
progression: Social-science, sustainability, data and research foundations precede advanced urban inequality, environmental governance, earth observation, econometrics and applied research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest pathway, this alternative replaces broad health, cognition and media coverage with a sustained Earth-systems, sustainability, cities, governance and political-economy spine.

trace: Introduces linked environmental, social and economic dimensions of sustainability in places.

routeSelection.route: Earth Sciences major with Consultancy for Sustainability as the Year 2 practice project
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the broad Bèta-gamma programme rather than a disciplinary major. None of the 21 formal majors is more representative of that generic identity without importing a UCR-fit preference, so the first major listed by the official programme, Earth Sciences, is selected before comparison. Where Project 2 offers two alternatives, the first listed option, Consultancy for Sustainability, is selected by the same rule.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the broad programme-defining interests and integrates science, society, humanities, research and communication. The two strongest coherent research-derived directions from the remaining generator interests are AI, Technology & Society and Sustainability, Cities & Public Policy; both pass the evidence, coherence, distinctness and feasibility gates. Cognition, Life, Health & Education and Society, Power, Culture & Resilience are coherent but cannot be added after the maximum of three alternatives is reached. Every schedule contains exactly 24 courses/180 EC, satisfies prerequisite and term constraints, and has substantial advanced-level depth.

notes.text: Bèta-gamma prescribes a common interdisciplinary first year and four cross-disciplinary projects before embedding 105 EC in a conventional disciplinary major. UCR instead builds one student-designed 180-EC Liberal Arts and Sciences curriculum from 24 courses, subject to progression and advanced-level requirements.

The official public curriculum gives the selected Earth Sciences major only as 51 EC in Year 2 and 54 EC in Year 3, with the thesis inside the latter total. Those aggregates are preserved rather than inventing course names or a thesis EC value.
The cited Bèta-gamma curriculum is Dutch-taught, whereas the UCR alternatives are English-taught.
